title: Project, stage, team and exception plans
blurb: Define the four PRINCE2 plans, say who creates and approves each, and explain how an exception plan replaces the plan it supersedes.
question: A stage is forecast to exceed its cost tolerance and the project board decides to address the exception. Which plan should the project manager now prepare?

teach.body: PRINCE2 recognizes four types of plan: the project plan, the stage plan, the team plan and the exception plan. Each is a proposal setting out the what, where, when, how and who, but for a different scope and at a different level of detail. Plain English: one big-picture plan for the whole project, a detailed plan for each stage, optional team plans for the work itself, and an exception plan when things go off course.

teach.caption: An exception plan sits beside the project plan or a stage plan and replaces it when approved. There are no exception plans for team plans.

teach.body: A high-level plan showing the project's major products and when, how and at what cost they will be delivered. The project manager creates it in initiating a project ('prepare the project plan'); it is baselined when the project board approves it in 'authorize the project'. It is updated at each stage boundary and at closure, and it identifies the proposed work packages, the top level of the work breakdown structure.

A stage plan is a detailed plan used as the basis for the project manager's control throughout a stage. The initiation stage plan is made in starting up a project; each later stage plan is prepared near the end of the current stage, in managing a stage boundary, so it is close to when the work happens. A team plan is produced by a team manager to organize and control a team's work on one or more work packages. Team plans are optional.

teach.h: Who prepares each plan, and when
head: Plan
Prepared by
Created in
Approved by
teach.caption: Stage plans and stage-level exception plans are approved in the DP activity 'authorize a stage or exception plan'.

teach.h: When the stage plans appear (three-stage project)
teach.caption: Two further stage plans follow the one made in SU. Closure is planned in the final stage plan, not as a separate stage.

teach.body: An exception plan follows an exception report. If the project board decides to address the exception, the project manager prepares an exception plan in managing a stage boundary. Once approved, it replaces the stage plan (or project plan) it covers, picking up from the current position to the end of that stage or project. Approval marks a stage boundary for the revised stage, so stage 2 becomes, in effect, stage 2a.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Ellery Housing's boiler upgrade
teach.body: At Ellery Housing Association, project manager Grace Obi runs a three-stage boiler upgrade. In stage 2 a supplier's price rise means the stage is forecast to exceed its cost tolerance. Grace sends an exception report; the board, chaired by executive Martin Hale, asks for an exception plan. Grace prepares it in managing a stage boundary. Once the board approves it, it replaces the stage 2 plan from that point on, and the team managers adjust their own optional team plans to suit.

teach.text: Three classic slips: the initiation stage plan is made in starting up a project, not in initiation; an exception plan is prepared in managing a stage boundary, not controlling a stage (CS is where the exception report is raised); and an exception plan never replaces a team plan, because work package problems are handled by the project manager.

items: Four plans: project, stage, team, exception.
Project plan: high level, created in IP, baselined when the board authorizes the project, updated at stage boundaries and closure.
Stage plan: detailed, basis of PM control; initiation stage plan in SU, later ones in SB near the end of the current stage.
Team plan: by a team manager for one or more work packages; optional.
Exception plan: follows an exception report, prepared in SB, replaces the stage or project plan from the current position.

summary: You can now define the project, stage, team and exception plans, say who prepares and approves each and in which process. You can also explain how an exception plan follows an exception report and replaces the stage or project plan it covers.

A.q: Which plan is a high-level plan showing the major products and when, how and at what cost they will be delivered?
A.why: The project plan is the high-level plan of major products, timing, method and cost (7.2.2.1).

whyNot.0: A stage plan is detailed and covers one stage.
whyNot.1: A team plan covers a team's work on one or more work packages.
whyNot.2: An exception plan responds to an exception report.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. A [?] plan is produced by a team manager to organize and control a team's work on one or more work packages, and is optional.
A.why: Team plans are produced by team managers for one or more work packages and are optional (7.2.2.3).

whyNot.0: Stage plans are prepared by the project manager for a whole stage.
whyNot.2: The project plan is prepared by the project manager for the whole project.
whyNot.3: Exception plans are prepared by the project manager after an exception report.

A.q: When is the initiation stage plan created?
A.why: The initiation stage plan is made in starting up a project ('plan the initiation stage'); later stage plans are made in managing a stage boundary (7.2.2.2, 13.4.7).

whyNot.1: Initiation needs its plan before it starts; the project plan, not the initiation stage plan, is created in IP.
whyNot.2: SB prepares the plans for the stages after initiation.
whyNot.3: The board approves the initiation stage plan in DP; it does not create it.

B.q:
Which two statements about the project plan are correct?
1. It is created in initiating a project.
2. It is baselined when the project board approves it.
3. It is prepared by a team manager for each work package.
4. It is replaced by the first stage plan once delivery begins.
B.why: The project plan is created in IP and baselined on approval by the board; it is then updated at stage boundaries and closure (7.2.2.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 3 is false: the project manager prepares the project plan; team managers may prepare team plans.
whyNot.1: Statement 4 is false: the project plan continues alongside stage plans and is updated at each stage boundary.
whyNot.2: Both are false: team managers do not prepare the project plan, and it is not replaced by stage plans.

B.q: Which plan is the basis for the project manager's day-to-day control throughout a stage?
B.why: A stage plan is a detailed plan used as the basis for project management control throughout a stage (7.2.2.2).

whyNot.0: The project plan is high level; it is the board's main control tool for the whole project.
whyNot.2: A team plan is the team manager's plan for work packages, and it is optional.
whyNot.3: PRINCE2 7 has no 'benefits plan'; benefits are covered by the business case and benefits management approach.

B.q: A project has three stages, including initiation. After starting up a project, how many further stage plans are needed?
B.why: The initiation stage plan is made in SU; the plans for stages 2 and 3 are made in SB near the end of the preceding stage, so two more are needed (7.2.2.2).

whyNot.0: One covers only stage 2; stage 3 also needs its own stage plan.
whyNot.1: Three would count the initiation stage plan again, which already exists from SU.
whyNot.3: There are only three stages, and closure is part of the final stage, not a stage needing its own plan.

C.q: A project board decides to address a forecast breach of stage tolerance. In which process is the exception plan prepared, and which plan does it replace?
options: Controlling a stage; it replaces the work package
Managing a stage boundary; it replaces the stage plan
Managing product delivery; it replaces the team plan
Directing a project; it replaces the project brief
C.why: Exception plans are prepared in SB ('prepare exception plan') and, once approved, replace the stage (or project) plan from the current position (7.2.2.4, ch 18).

whyNot.0: CS is where the exception report is raised; the plan itself is prepared in SB, and work packages are not replaced by exception plans.
whyNot.2: Exception plans are never produced for team plans, and MP is the team manager's process.
whyNot.3: The board decides and approves in DP; the project brief belongs to starting up a project.

C.q: Which statement about an exception plan is correct?
options: It is prepared by a team manager when work package tolerance is at risk
It is prepared before the exception report so the board sees both together
It follows an exception report and picks up from the current position
It is added to the existing stage plan, which stays in force alongside it
C.why: An exception plan follows an exception report and, once approved, replaces the plan it covers from the current position to its end (7.2.2.4).

whyNot.0: Forecast work package breaches go to the project manager as an issue; exception plans are prepared by the project manager for stage or project plans.
whyNot.1: The board first receives the exception report and then decides whether to ask for an exception plan.
whyNot.3: The exception plan replaces the stage plan rather than running alongside it.

C.q: During stage 2 of a four-stage project, who prepares the plan for stage 3, and when?
options: The project manager, near the end of stage 2
The team manager, at the start of stage 3
C.why: Later stage plans are prepared by the project manager in managing a stage boundary near the end of the current stage, close to when the work happens (7.2.2.2).

whyNot.1: Team managers may produce team plans, not stage plans, and the stage plan must be approved before stage 3 starts.
whyNot.2: Planning stage 3 in detail during initiation goes beyond the planning horizon; IP produces the project plan.
whyNot.3: The executive approves stage plans; the project manager prepares them.

reteach.title: Map, street plan and to-do list
reteach.question: How are the project plan, stage plan and team plan like a road atlas, a street plan and a delivery driver's list?

blocks.body: The project plan is the road atlas: the whole route, major waypoints, rough timings and cost. Each stage plan is the street plan for the next leg, drawn just before you drive it. A team plan is a driver's own list of drops, used if the team wants one. If a road closure means the leg can no longer be finished within tolerance, you replace the street plan with a new one: the exception plan.

blocks.text: Exception plans replace stage or project plans only after the board approves them. They are never prepared for team plans or work packages.

explain.body: High level: major products, when, how and at what cost. Created in IP, baselined when the board authorizes the project, updated in SB and CP.

test.q: When is the project plan baselined?
options: When the first work package is accepted
When the board authorizes the project
When the first end stage report is approved
test.why: The project plan is created in IP and baselined on approval by the project board in 'authorize the project' (7.2.2.1).

whyNot.0: When initiation is authorized, the project plan does not yet exist; it is created during initiation.
whyNot.1: Work packages are accepted in MP, long after the project plan is baselined.
whyNot.3: By the first end stage report the project plan has already been baselined; it is then updated.

explain.body: Detailed plans for the project manager's control of one stage. The initiation stage plan is made in SU; the rest in SB near the end of the current stage. Closure activities are planned in the final stage plan.

explain.h: Where is this stage plan made?

test.q: Where should the activities for closing a project be planned?
options: In a separate closure stage plan
In the stage plan for the final stage
In the team plan of the final team to finish
In an exception plan for closure
test.why: Closure activities are planned as part of the stage plan for the final stage; closing a project is not a stage (7.2.2.2, ch 18).

whyNot.0: Closing a project runs inside the final stage, so there is no separate closure stage.
whyNot.2: Team plans cover work packages, not project closure.
whyNot.3: Exception plans respond to exceptions, not planned closure.

explain.body: Produced by a team manager to organize and control the team's work on one or more work packages. PRINCE2 treats them as optional.

test.q: Which statement about team plans is correct?
options: They are approved by the project board in DP
They are prepared by the project manager
They can be replaced by exception plans
test.why: Team plans are produced by team managers for one or more work packages and are optional (7.2.2.3).

whyNot.0: The board approves stage and exception plans in DP; team plans sit within the team manager's work.
whyNot.2: Exception plans are not produced for team plans.

explain.body: Follow an exception report when the board decides to address the exception. Prepared in SB, approved by the board, they replace the stage or project plan from the current position.

test.q: What does an exception plan follow?
test.why: An exception plan follows an exception report, if the board decides to address the exception (7.2.2.4).

whyNot.0: An issue report covers an issue handled formally, often within tolerance.
whyNot.1: Checkpoint reports go from team manager to project manager on work package status.
whyNot.2: Highlight reports give the board regular stage status, not exceptions.
